subject: Post-call: speed triage + proposed AB matrix vs hyperscaler
body:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: speed triage + proposed AB matrix vs hyperscaler

Claire — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: we heard your team's primary risk is latency spikes during peak batch ingest and inconsistent p99s across the hyperscaler endpoint you tested. You asked for a short, low-friction A/B that isolates the differences and gives clear pass/fail criteria for SRE.

High-level proposal (attached: bench-plan-v1.csv + redwood-interop-matrix.pdf):
- A/B targets: Redwood hosted API (our production build) vs Hyperscaler inference endpoint (your PoC account).
- Workloads: 3 slices — short chat (50-150 tokens), mid context (300-1k tokens), long context (1k-3k tokens).
- Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (steady-state and peak), 95th-99th latency when concurrency=16/64/128, error-rate and tail retry (%)
- Run cadence: 24-hour steady run + 1-hour microburst window to exercise queueing and batching behavior.
- Pass criteria (example): p95 < 400ms for short slice; p99 < 1.5s for short slice; tokens/sec within 15% of expected throughput baseline for mid slice. We can tighten once we see baseline numbers.

Requests from Acme:
1) Share a small sample of real-ish payloads (we discussed ~500 sample prompts, anonymized) — filename OK as acme_sample_payloads.zip.
2) Provide Hyperscaler PoC credentials for test account (read-only) or a short-lived API key so we can run identical scripts against both endpoints.

Next steps / owners:
- Ben: create the A/B harness and run initial smoke tests once we get payloads + credentials (ETA: 48 hours after access).
- Marissa: coordinate legal if we need a short PoC Addendum for elevated rate limits (she'll ping procurement).
- Sergio: draft a 1-page SRE readout with the acceptance matrix for your infra team.

Attachments referenced: bench-plan-v1.csv (test matrix), redwood-interop-matrix.pdf (how we map quantization/batching profiles to model variants).

If that matches what you need, we can start as soon as you drop the sample payloads and the Hyperscaler PoC key.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0142

From: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: speed triage + proposed AB matrix vs hyperscaler

Ben — this looks great, thanks. Two clarifications: first, the Hyperscaler PoC key will be scoped to their 'low-latency' endpoint (they gave us a temporary token for initial tests). Second, our mid-context workload includes a pre- and post-processing step on our side (tokenization + post-filtering) that currently adds ~30-50ms — we should compare raw inference times only.

I'll upload the anonymized samples (acme_sample_payloads.zip) to the shared Drive you linked. For credentials I can either drop the token in the Drive (zipped) or create a service account for you — which do you prefer?

Claire
Claire Jensen
PM, Acme Corp
claire.jensen@acme.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2029 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: speed triage + proposed AB matrix vs hyperscaler

Claire — thanks, Drive upload is perfect. If it's easy for you to create a scoped service account (short TTL) that's our preference — avoids manual token rotation during the run. Either way will work. We'll strip pre/post-processing and measure pure inference latency; we'll also publish a small harness so you can reproduce runs.

Marissa / Sergio — looping you in for the legal/ops notes: Marissa, an addendum for temporary elevated rate limits (two-week PoC) — can you draft a short note? Sergio, once we have the token we'll kick off the smoke tests and I'll share the harness.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2029 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: speed triage + proposed AB matrix vs hyperscaler

Claire — drafting the PoC addendum now. A couple notes from a readiness point:
- We recommend the first run focus on single-model parity (same model family / same quantization profile). Hyperscaler often uses larger default VMs which can mask batching inefficiencies. Pinning model variant avoids noisy comparisons.
- We'll include instructions to disable platform-side auto-scaling and to fix concurrency targets during the run so the results are comparable.
- For observability, please share a single representative trace for a p99 event if you have one recorded — it helps us triage where tail latency arises.

I attached a rough redwood-interop-matrix.pdf that maps the configs we typically test (batch window, batching threshold, KV cache warmup, fp16 vs int8 quant).

I'll get the addendum over by EOD PT.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-interop-matrix.pdf

From: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@acme.com>

Date: Wed, 29 May 2029 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: speed triage + proposed AB matrix vs hyperscaler

Thanks all — I uploaded acme_sample_payloads.zip to the Drive folder and created a short-lived service account for the PoC under the name acme-redwood-test. I also included a single app trace for a p99 spike (trace-20290521.json) — hope helpful.

Ben — go ahead with the smoke tests. We'll plan a 48-hour window next week for the full A/B run once Sergio confirms the fixed concurrency config on our side.

Claire

[End of thread]
